title: Number of Unique XOR Triplets II
summary: Given an integer array, count the distinct results of the XOR operation applied to all possible triplets of elements where the indices follow the order i <= j <= k.
statement: Given an integer array, count the distinct results of the XOR operation applied to all possible triplets of elements where the indices follow the order i <= j <= k.
constraints: nums has 1 to 1,500 positive integers, each at most 1,500.
A triplet value is nums[i] XOR nums[j] XOR nums[k] for indices i <= j <= k; repeated indices are allowed.
Return the number of distinct values among all such triplets.
hints: Because XOR is commutative and indices may repeat, choosing any three array values can be reordered into nondecreasing indices.
First enumerate every reachable pair XOR, then combine each pair value with every input value.
Build a set of a XOR b, then a set of pair XOR c, and return its size.
The first set represents all two-choice prefixes and the second represents exactly every legal triplet value, with sets removing duplicates.
editorial: The first set represents all two-choice prefixes and the second represents exactly every legal triplet value, with sets removing duplicates.

tests.explanation: The four ordered-index choices produce only values one and three, so the answer is two.
Although many triplets exist, their XOR results collapse to four distinct values.
